# Conflict states

Generated by the state test (`go test -run TestStates -update`); do not edit.

## Axes

- **kind**: new, changed, gone
- **target**: none, some
- **ready**: blocked, ready

## Rules

| rule | bucket | reason | why | resolved by / guarded by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| edit-not-applied | contradiction | fix | She changed or deleted an event in the calendar in a way bizzy doesn't allow | calendar.revert, conflicts.apply |
| edit-ready | contradiction | fix | An edit she made in the calendar is allowed now: something done since lets it through, maybe for another reason, so it waits for her to apply it rather than applying by itself | conflicts.apply, calendar.revert |
| event-not-read | contradiction | fix | A new event in the calendar can't be read as a session or follow-up | calendar.ignore, conflicts.apply |
| new-with-target | impossible |  | A new record shows nothing of bizzy's yet, and a known one always does | by construction: the sync keys a conflict by what the record showed when she changed it |
| new-ready | impossible |  | A new event is read as soon as nothing refuses it | by construction: the sync applies a new event whenever it reads it (googlesync's try) |

## States

12 combinations of the axes. 7 are impossible (an impossible rule holds) and left out. The 5 reachable ones (5 contradiction, 0 needs-action, 0 quiet) are shown as 5 rows, `*` meaning any value.

| kind | target | ready | bucket | reasons | rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| new | none | blocked | contradiction | fix | event-not-read |
| changed | some | blocked | contradiction | fix | edit-not-applied |
| changed | some | ready | contradiction | fix | edit-ready |
| gone | some | blocked | contradiction | fix | edit-not-applied |
| gone | some | ready | contradiction | fix | edit-ready |
